impacts.text: Any user with no special permissions can repeatedly call `rebalanceFunds` to keep the buffer close to its target, reducing the likelihood that large redemptions can be served from the vault.
Those redemptions are instead routed to the custodian path, which is inherently slower and dependent on off‑chain actions, contradicting the design goal of a “Fast Access Vault”.

An attacker can monitor the mempool and call `rebalanceFunds` just before large redemptions are included in a block, systematically forcing them into the custodian path despite ample on‑chain liquidity being available at the time users submitted their transactions.
This can lead to miscalibrated off‑chain behavior (e.g., sending funds in response to an event triggered by an attacker, or misinterpreting vault state).
it materially weakens the protocol’s liquidity guarantees
gives an unprivileged party a lever to sabotage user redemptions

ambiguities: Redemptions may be forced down the `_redeemFromCustodian` path (e_18114238d594_0015) is stated as a potential consequence and overlaps with the routed-to-custodian-path outcome.
